data.title: Fragmented Signal
data.statement:
A damaged communication system has recovered a transmission, but the original message is no longer available.

Before transmission, the message was processed through a sequence of reversible transformations. The system recorded the transformations, but unfortunately, it only stored them in the order in which they were originally applied.

Your task is to reconstruct the original message.

Every operation described below is reversible. However, because the operations were applied sequentially, they must be undone in reverse order.

For example, if the original message was processed using:

A → B → C

the reconstruction must perform:

undo C → undo B → undo A

The recovered message must be output exactly as it originally appeared.
data.constraints:
10 ≤ length([[S]]) ≤ 100
1 ≤ [[N]] ≤ 10
0 ≤ [[a]] < length([[S]])
0 ≤ [[b]] < length([[S]])
[[a]] ≠ [[b]]
1 ≤ [[k]] < length([[S]])

For {{B}} [[k]], the length of [[S]] is divisible by [[k]].
For {{P}}, the length of [[S]] is divisible by 4.

<<Line 1:>> A string [[S]], representing the transformed message.

<<Line 2:>> An integer [[N]], the number of operations applied to the original message.

Next [[N]] lines: One operation per line, listed in the order in which they were originally applied.

Each operation is one of the following:

* {{R}}: Reverse the entire string.
* {{L}} [[k]]: Rotate the string left by [[k]] positions.
* {{S}} [[a]] [[b]]: Swap the characters at positions [[a]] and [[b]] (0-based indexed).
* {{B}} [[k]]: Divide the string into [[k]] equal-sized blocks and reverse the order of the blocks.
* {{P}}: Divide the string into groups of 4 characters and swap the first two characters with the last two characters in each group.
data.outputDescription:
The original transmission, reconstructed by undoing all [[N]] transformations in reverse order.

The output must contain the exact sequence of characters that was present before the first transformation was applied.

Do not add or remove any characters.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

A damaged communication system has recovered a transmission, but the original message is no longer available.

Before transmission, the message was processed through a sequence of reversible transformations. The system recorded the transformations, but unfortunately, it only stored them in the order in which they were originally applied.

Your task is to reconstruct the original message.

Every operation described below is reversible. However, because the operations were applied sequentially, they must be undone in reverse order.

For example, if the original message was processed using:

A → B → C

the reconstruction must perform:

undo C → undo B → undo A

The recovered message must be output exactly as it originally appeared.
Input
Line 1: A string S, representing the transformed message.

Line 2: An integer N, the number of operations applied to the original message.

Next N lines: One operation per line, listed in the order in which they were originally applied.

Each operation is one of the following:

* R: Reverse the entire string.
* L k: Rotate the string left by k positions.
* S a b: Swap the characters at positions a and b (0-based indexed).
* B k: Divide the string into k equal-sized blocks and reverse the order of the blocks.
* P: Divide the string into groups of 4 characters and swap the first two characters with the last two characters in each group.
Output
The original transmission, reconstructed by undoing all N transformations in reverse order.

The output must contain the exact sequence of characters that was present before the first transformation was applied.

Do not add or remove any characters.
Constraints
10 ≤ length(S) ≤ 100
1 ≤ N ≤ 10
0 ≤ a < length(S)
0 ≤ b < length(S)
a ≠ b
1 ≤ k < length(S)

For B k, the length of S is divisible by k.
For P, the length of S is divisible by 4.
Example
Input
ECNELISGNOLRETFADEVIECERLANGISDETNEMGARF
1
R
Output
FRAGMENTEDSIGNALRECEIVEDAFTERLONGSILENCE
